title: Library stays open late for young readers
text:
Mawar Town Library began a new service on Monday evening: a free reading hour for children, from six o'clock to seven o'clock on weekdays. Until now, the library has closed at five. This meant that many pupils with after-school clubs could not borrow books.

Librarian Ibu Sari said that about forty children came on the first night. "Some of them sat on the floor and read for the whole hour," she said. "I have worked here for twelve years, and I have never seen the children's section so busy."

The idea came from a group of pupils at Mawar Primary School. Last term, they wrote to the town council to ask for later opening times. The council agreed to pay for one extra member of staff, Mr Budi, who will look after the children's section during the new hour. The service will be tested for three months. If enough children come, it will become permanent.

Not everybody is happy. Mr Rahman, who lives next door to the library, says the extra hour will make the street too noisy. "Children should be at home doing their homework at that time," he said. Ibu Sari disagrees. "A library is the quietest place in town," she said. "A hundred children reading make less noise than one motorbike."

Parents who wish to sign up their children can do so at the front desk. Library cards are free for everyone under sixteen.
